# Worked examples {#c06-worked-examples}

This chapter moves from data preparation to research questions.

Each example starts with a question that researchers might genuinely ask of MICS6 Foundational Learning Skills data and then works through the population being studied, the variables required, the survey design, the analysis, a suggested visualisation, and the interpretation.

The examples use the AFLEARN harmonised selected-child and reading files developed in [Preparing UNICEF data](#c03-prepare-unicef) and [Preparing IPUMS data](#c04-prepare-ipums).

| Example | Question |
|---|---|
| [Prepare the analysis data](#c06-prepare-analysis) | How do I create one survey-ready analysis file? |
| [Who is assessed?](#c06-who-assessed) | Who is represented in the FLS sample? |
| [Indicators versus distributions](#c06-numeracy-distributions) | What do we lose when we report only the headline numeracy indicator? |
| [Missing reading outcomes](#c06-reading-status) | Why does a child have no reading score? |
| [Reading language and coverage](#c06-reading-language) | Who is assessed in which language, and who cannot be assessed? |
| [Learning inequalities by wealth](#c06-wealth) | Do proficiency indicators reveal the same inequalities as score distributions? |
| [In-school and out-of-school children](#c06-schooling-status) | How does learning differ by current school attendance at the same age? |
| [Learning by grade and age](#c06-grade-trajectories) | How does performance change across grades, and how does age complicate interpretation? |
| [Timing within the school year](#c06-school-timing) | Are children labelled as the same grade equally far through that grade? |

Each page includes both R and Stata code. The complete scripts are also provided as `Script/worked-examples.R` and `Script/worked-examples.do`. The scripts are templates. They use actual AFLEARN harmonised variable names where those names are already fixed in the current processing scripts.

A small number of variables still require additions or merges: survey-design variables are covered in [Prepare the analysis data](#c06-prepare-analysis), and wealth in [Learning inequalities by wealth](#c06-wealth).

::: {.alternativebox-header}
**Run the code; do not copy the example interpretation**
:::

::: {.alternativebox}
The text explains what to look for. Numerical findings and graph-specific interpretation should be written only after running the code on the final harmonised datasets.
:::

The examples demonstrate sound ways to use MICS6 data. They are not intended to prescribe one preferred outcome for every research question. In particular, AFLEARN encourages researchers to look beyond binary foundational-learning indicators when the underlying item-level data answer the question more directly.

The MICS6 FLS module contains the individual numeracy items and detailed reading information required for this type of analysis, while the household-survey design allows learning to be studied among both in-school and out-of-school children.
